chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prayed over Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and said: 'Ninety thousand angels, including Jibreel (peace be upon him), attended his funeral prayer.' I asked him, 'O Jibreel, for what reason did you deserve to pray over him?' He replied, 'Because of his recitation of
Say, He is Allah, [who is] One.
While standing, sitting, riding, walking, going, and coming.'

key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ مُعَاذٍ: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, a companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Why did Jibreel pray over Sa'd ibn Mu'adh?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the immense spiritual merit of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas, linking it to the specific honor of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq questioning the Archangel Jibreel during the funeral prayer for Sa'd ibn Mu'adh. The text emphasizes that the reward stems from the consistency of this recitation across all states of being—standing, sitting, riding, and walking—demonstrating its integration into daily life. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that the concise declaration of divine unity carries weight comparable to a third of the Quran, warranting such celestial attention.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 6. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan who said it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan al-Saffar from Ibrahim b. Hashim from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Ja’far b. Muhammad from his father (a.s.) who said: “

His funeral prayer was attended by ninety thousand angels accompanied by Jibraeel (a.s.). I asked Jibraeel (a.s.), ‘Why did you people attend this funeral prayer?’ Jibraeel (a.s.) replied, ‘He used to recite Surah Tauheed
standing or sitting, riding or walking and while coming and going’.”
